tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description uses imperative phrasing ('Use this skill when...'), focuses on user-facing symptoms (job fails, times out, scores only part of input, whether to use batch vs endpoint) rather than internal implementation, and explicitly lists trigger contexts including cases where the user doesn't name the domain terms directly ('even if they do not mention JSON Lines, SplitType...'). It is a dense but single, well-structured paragraph, which is reasonable given the breadth of symptoms it must cover.
tests.evidence: Use this skill when the user ... and when someone asks whether a large periodic scoring run should use batch transform or a real-time endpoint, or whether scored output is protected, even if they do not mention JSON Lines, SplitType, MaxPayloadInMB, ModelClientConfig, JoinSource, MaxConcurrentTransforms or KMS keys by name.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile/irreversible operations (guardrails, read-only enforcement, check-id assignment) are prescriptive, while flexible areas (break-fix diagnosis, which API to call first) explain reasoning and allow judgment, matching prescriptiveness to fragility.
tests.evidence: 1. **Read-only.** Never call a transform mutation (`CreateTransformJob`) or any other mutating API. Recommend the fix and give the exact CLI/IaC command; let the user run it.

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: The skill does not present multiple competing tools for the same task as equal choices; it routes to a single canonical API/check path per symptom via the Router table.

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The skill teaches a generalizable diagnostic procedure (match symptom to check-id, confirm with API calls, report with severity) applicable to any batch transform job, not a one-off instance.
tests.evidence: Match the symptom, confirm with the collection calls, then report with the check-id and severity from the catalog.
